newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds closed higher on Friday after an active session.
Comments from Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke on a possible cut in the German repurchase rate in the mid-term gave a boost to the major bond markets.
But soon after Spain's official close, Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said he did not see any reason for further rate cuts in foreseeable future.
"The level of 107.50 triggered short-covering," said Miguel Angel Lopez dealer at Fimat in Madrid. He put next resistance at 107.99 and support at 107.42 and then 107.26.
The 10-year spread over German Bunds narrowed to 171 basis points from 178 bps in early trade. "We do not expect a big change in the level of the spread in the near term," a dealer in Madrid said.
With little domestic news on the agenda for next week, Spanish bonds are likely to track other foreign markets, he added.
Dealers said the yield curve was still relatively flat.
"We expect some steepening in the coming days," one dealer said. The 7.80 percent three year bond closed the day around 107.06 from 106.44, yield 7.70 percent.
